title: Inquest called into Taser death
article: An inquest has begun into the death of a Winnipeg teen who suffered a fatal heart attack after police shocked him with a Taser.
Michael Brian Langan, 17, died July 22, 2008 following a confrontation with police in the alley between the 800-block of William Avenue and the National Microbiology Lab.
Taser International lawyer David Neave said the company will be "taking serious issue" with a medical examiner's report concluding the Taser device was responsible for Langan's death.
"We will be cross-examining at length on those statements and documents," Neave told inquest Judge Tim Killeen.
Court heard Langan was suspected of having broken into a car outside MWG Apparel Corp on Notre Dame Avenue when he came "face-to-face" with the car's owner, MWG owner Hartley Klapman.
Klapman said the young man was holding a binocular case that had been stored in his trunk.

"He was jumping around in an agitated state, like a boxer," Klapman testified. "He said 'Do you want me or do you want the purse?' ... In other words, 'Do you want to fight me or take the purse and call it a day?'"
Klapman took the binocular case and then turned to assess the damage to his car as Langan took off on foot.
MWG employee Henry Connon called 911 and followed Langan, the inquest heard.
Klapman said he drove after Connon, fearing for his safety. Klapman said he caught up to Connon on McPhillips Street and saw Langan on the other side of the road.
"He made a physical gesture toward us, as if to say he had gotten away," Klapman said. "It would have gotten my adrenaline going."
The two men lost sight of Langan for a time before catching up to him in a Bannatyne Avenue back lane where Klapman tried to box him in between a fence and a utility trailer.
Langan produced a knife, held it over his head and said "Are you trying to kill me?" Klapman testified.
Langan escaped and the men followed him to William Avenue where they flagged down a police cruiser.
Connon said he followed police on foot to a William Avenue back lane where they cornered Langan between a fence and a garage.
Connon said one officer ordered him to stay back as the other positioned himself behind the cruiser passenger door and aimed what Connon thought was a Taser in Langan's direction.
"At that point the officer told the individual to drop his weapon," Connon said. "He repeated it again, said 'Drop your f...... knife.'"
Connon said he didn't hear Langan respond. "I heard a 'poop' and that was it. I saw these two wires protrude from the Taser.
Connon said all he could see of Langan were his shoes after he fell to the ground about five feet from the police cruiser.
"Next thing I hear is the driver calling for assistance, for an ambulance," he said.
The inquest continues.
